answer: A verifiable delay tax resists sybils. A new identity cannot answer until it proves that a fixed sequential computation ran from its registration seed, bound to the current epoch so it cannot be precomputed and replayed. The delay is serial, so an attacker wanting a thousand identities must wait a thousand times longer or buy a thousand times the hardware, and cost scales with clones. Each proof stays an echo of its seed, so reuse leaves a trace. An honest agent pays once and answers freely, while a fake lotus must be built petal by petal; at a wharf, more hulls never hurry the tide.
